source.title: GQLA: Group-Query Latent Attention for Hardware-Adaptive Decoding

record.tranche_reason: The study fits power laws to compute and terminal training loss, but its loss measure differs from the claim’s held-out pretraining loss.
record.gate_note: The scaling experiment reports terminal training loss averaged over the final 100 iterations and explicitly says it does not measure held-out or downstream quality. It does not validate its dashed extrapolations against larger runs. Conversion, kernel, and serving results do not test the scaling-law versions. The paper cites scaling-law work, but cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses a power law with an additive constant as a descriptive tool to compare MLA and GQLA attention under one pretraining recipe. Its measure is terminal training loss (mean of the final 100 iterations). The authors state this is not held-out or downstream quality. They also say the fits do not establish asymptotic laws or compute-optimal training, and the dashed extrapolations are never checked against larger runs. So no version is tested; the scaling result serves the architecture comparison. The reader's 'tests/T2' contradicts its own 'not_tested' status for every version.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct: GQLA's terminal training losses are close to MLA's over the tested scales. The authors caution that the fits do not establish equal asymptotic laws, held-out quality, compute-optimal training or downstream generalization.
record.recipe_differences: This is an architecture comparison using terminal training loss, not a reproduction of the original held-out-loss scaling measurements. It fits a power law with an additive constant to a small set of architecture-specific compute estimates.
record.method_sensitivity: The compute curves depend on architecture-specific FLOP estimates. The study uses independent unweighted nonlinear least-squares fits; it does not vary fitting choices to measure sensitivity.

fits_no_version.finding: Under a shared MoE pretraining recipe, MLA and GQLA show near-identical fitted compute exponents for terminal training loss (alpha 0.123 vs 0.124). The matched-token gap between them narrows with scale, from 0.0184 to 0.0041.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grouping KV up-projections in latent attention (8 query heads per group) costs little training loss, and the cost shrinks with scale over the tested range.

record.problems: The scaling evidence is terminal training loss, not held-out loss. MLA and GQLA 1:8 each have six endpoints, while GQLA 1:4 has four; fits have no reported uncertainty intervals, and GQLA 1:4 has only one residual degree of freedom. The study says the dashed extrapolations do not establish asymptotic laws. The endpoints are not independent repeated runs, and the compute axis uses architecture-specific FLOP estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No scaling rows omitted. Figure-only endpoint values were not transcribed as exact numbers because the text does not state them; the reported fit exponents and textual gap comparisons are recorded instead.

untested.parts: Held-out loss is not measured; only terminal training loss is reported, and the fit is descriptive.
The extrapolations to 1e23 FLOPs are not validated against larger runs.
No depth or width comparison at a fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime is tested with a scaling fit.
No downstream measure is related to scale or loss.

record.verdict_notes: Main contributions are attention-architecture design, checkpoint conversion and kernel/serving speedups, none bearing on the scaling claim. Endpoint loss values appear only in Figure 4. The compute axis uses architecture-specific FLOP estimates. There is one seed and no repeated runs.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining loss; the study measures terminal training loss instead.
No measured larger runs are compared with predictions fitted on smaller runs; plotted extrapolations are not validated.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture details at fixed parameter count.
No other modalities, repeated-data regimes, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law test.
No downstream-performance scaling test against scale or pretraining loss.
The study specifies its fitting method and notes limits on interpreting its fits, but does not vary fitting choices or test compute-optimal allocation to establish setup dependence.

rows.subject: MLA
rows.operation_detail: Fit terminal training loss against estimated cumulative training compute with a power law plus additive constant.

conditions.value: three parameters; unweighted nonlinear least squares in loss space

rows.measure: Fitted compute-loss power-law exponent α for terminal training loss
rows.note: The fit is descriptive for the measured training-loss endpoints; the study says this does not establish an asymptotic law.
rows.check: Descriptive fit of training loss, not held-out loss, on six endpoints with no uncertainty reported. It is a tool for architecture comparison, not a test of V1. The link to 'none' is correct.

rows.subject: GQLA 1:8
rows.operation_detail: Compare terminal training loss with MLA at matched token budget.

rows.note: The text reports this as the gap at the smallest scale; individual loss values are not stated.
